bibliographic.title: The Global Integrated World Ocean Assessment: Linking Observations to Science and Policy Across Multiple Scales
bibliographic.authors: Karen Evans, Sanae Chiba, Maria J. Bebianno, Carlos Garcia-Soto, Henn Ojaveer, Chul Park, Renison Ruwa, Alan J. Simcock, C. T. Vu, Tymon Zielinski
bibliographic.citation_apa: Evans, K., Chiba, S., Bebianno, M. J., Garcia-Soto, C., Ojaveer, H., Park, C., Ruwa, R., Simcock, A. J., Vu, C. T., & Zielinski, T. (2019). The Global Integrated World Ocean Assessment: Linking Observations to Science and Policy Across Multiple Scales. Frontiers in Marine Science, 6, 298. https://doi.org/10.3389/fmars.2019.00298

methodology.method_family: integrated environmental assessment and science-policy knowledge brokering
methodology.study_design: community white paper reviewing the UN Regular Process for Global Reporting and Assessment of the State of the Marine Environment (World Ocean Assessment)
methodology.sample_description: Ocean observation community, managers, policy makers, and regional stakeholders contributing to the World Ocean Assessment process
methodology.technology_context: ocean observation and monitoring systems, modeling frameworks, citizen science, sustained observation systems

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article discusses global marine environment assessment and linking ocean observations to science and policy; it does not address LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, or conversational governance.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Deterministic triage matched terms such as dialogue, trust, policy, government, education, monitoring, and deployment, but the provided text shows these refer to stakeholder dialogue, marine policy, capacity building, and observation-system deployment in ocean assessment—not to governance of LLM-based conversational systems. No evidence of chatbots, agents, RAG, guardrails, audit/logging for AI, human oversight of AI outputs, or regulated-domain conversational AI.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic mismatch is explicit in title and abstract; keyword overlap with review scope is contextual rather than technological.

appraisal.notes: As a policy-oriented review/white paper on ocean assessment, objectives and policy linkages are reasonably clear, but empirical sampling, data collection, and analysis methods are not described in the provided excerpts. Appraisal is secondary because the study is out of scope for the review question.

cerqual.explanation: For the review question on conversational governance of LLM systems in regulated settings, relevance is effectively absent. Provided text supports a coherent account of marine science-policy assessment but offers no findings applicable to conversational AI governance.

coding.subtheme: World Ocean Assessment process and stakeholder engagement

synthesis.main_claim: The World Ocean Assessment links ocean observation and research to management and policy needs across local, regional, and global scales through integrated assessment and knowledge brokering.
synthesis.contribution: Describes how the UN Regular Process uses observations, regional workshops, stakeholder dialogue, and capacity building to assess marine environmental state and trends and inform policy makers.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central or supporting evidence; at most marginal contextual reference for generic science-policy governance, not conversational or LLM governance.
